guideTitle: 6 Best Non Slip Shower Mats for Seniors in 2026
metaTitle: Best Non Slip Shower Mats for Seniors 2026
metaDescription: Six non slip shower mats for older adults compared on edge flatness, cushioning, visibility, easy cleaning and how well each stays put under wet feet.
mainKeyword: non slip shower mat for elderly
introParagraphs: For an older adult, a shower mat does a slightly different job than it does for a younger household. It still needs to stop sliding, but it also needs to be easy to see against the tub, soft enough not to hurt tender feet, flat enough at the edges that it does not catch a toe and simple enough for someone else to lift out and wash. A mat that fails any of those can end up rolled in a closet or, worse, left in place when it is not gripping.

The six picks are the GORILLA GRIP square stall mat at 21 by 21 inches, the Hargiis 0.4-inch thick loofah-surface mat, the OTHWAY with 198 suction cups and 360 drain holes, the TEMIR that cites ASTM F462 wet-surface testing, the TEESHLY 40 by 16 inch mat and the homerella with over 250 cups and a mildew-resistant design.

We evaluated each on grip, cushioning, size, visibility, cleaning and what the listing says about surfaces. This is about ease of use and comfort, not a medical claim, and no mat can guarantee against a slip, so we recommend combining a mat with a grab bar and a therapist's advice where there are specific mobility needs.

products.name: GORILLA GRIP Square Shower Stall Mat, 21x21 Clear
products.description:
Most mats in this category are long rectangles for tubs, but many older adults shower in a stand-up stall, where a 21 by 21 inch square fits the floor better. GORILLA GRIP's square mat uses hundreds of suction cups and hundreds of drainage holes, a hexagon pebble-textured top and BPA-free materials. It is a standing platform for the spot under the showerhead.

A square mat fits a stall's footprint, which keeps the edges away from the walls where they can curl. The pebble top gives bare feet a grippy surface without being harsh, and drainage holes keep water from pooling. The clear finish is subtle on the floor, so check that you can see it against the stall base, and the listing does not state a cup count in the text we have.

Compared with the long tub mats it is built for a stall, and compared with the OTHWAY it is smaller and from a known brand. It suits an older adult who showers standing in a stall with a smooth floor. If someone helps with bathing, a square mat is also easy for a second person to lift and replace.
products.bestFor: Stand-up stalls where a small square mat fits the floor.
pros: Square 21 by 21 in fits stall floors
Pebble-textured top is gentle on feet
cons: Cup count is not stated in the text we have
Small size gives little room to shift stance
Needs a smooth, non-porous stall floor

products.name: Hargiis Non Slip Bathtub Mat, 0.4 Inch Thick, Fast Drying
products.description:
Hargiis is the cushioned choice: a 0.4-inch thick mat in BPA-free PVC with a loofah-like foam top the listing says gives a comfortable, soft support for the feet and a gentle scrub, and a plaid-patterned backing that grips the floor. It is fast drying, and the listing says it rinses clean with a spray because the foam top washes off easily. It is described as a non-slip mat for tubs and showers.

A thicker, softer surface helps people with tender soles who find hard pebbles uncomfortable, and the foam top does not trap soap the way some textured designs do. The listing describes the backing as plaid rather than suction cups, so how well it grips depends on the tub floor, and the grip claim is the maker's. Check the full product page for the grip mechanism and surface notes.

Compared with the suction-cup mats it relies on a patterned backing, and compared with the TEESHLY it is thicker and softer. It suits someone who wants a cushioned feel and easy rinsing and is willing to verify the grip on their tub. If you choose it, press it flat and confirm that the plaid backing is not sliding before each shower.
products.bestFor: Tender feet and easy rinse-off cleaning.
cons: Grip comes from a patterned backing, not stated suction cups
Foam top may wear with use
Check the grip on your tub surface

products.name: OTHWAY Non Slip Bath Tub Shower Mat, 198 Suction Cups, 360 Drain Holes
products.description:
OTHWAY states its counts plainly: 198 high-density suction cups and 360 precision-angled drain holes in a flexible TPE body with raised nodules. For a caregiver comparing options for a parent, specific numbers are easier to work with than adjectives. The soft TPE flexes with the tub floor and the nodules give a gentle texture underfoot.

Fast drainage helps hygiene, since less standing water means less mildew, and a mat that is easy to keep clean is one that gets cleaned. The flexibility is a plus on a floor with a slight curve, but TPE can be a little slippery when coated in soap film, so rinse it regularly. The listing does not state dimensions in the text we have, so measure before ordering.

Compared with the TEMIR it gives counts instead of a standard, and compared with the homerella it has more holes but fewer cups. It suits a household that likes stated numbers and wants a flexible, quick-draining mat. A quick weekly rinse of the underside keeps the cups clean, which helps them keep their hold.
products.bestFor: A flexible mat with stated cup and hole counts.
cons: Dimensions are not stated in the text we have
Soap film can make TPE slick if not rinsed

products.name: TEMIR Non Slip Bathtub Mat, ASTM F462 Tested, Suction Cups

specList.label: Testing
specList.value: ASTM F462 wet-surface slip, per listing

products.description:
TEMIR cites independent testing in a U.S.-based accredited lab following ASTM F462 wet-surface slip resistance guidelines, alongside strong suction cups for smooth tub and shower bases, quick drain holes and a soft textured surface. For a family choosing a mat for a parent, a named test is a data point to read. The listing is also clear that the mat is designed for clean, smooth surfaces.

The test claim is the maker's statement, so treat it as design intent and check its scope on the product page. A soft, textured surface aims for grip without roughness, which matters for older feet, and machine washing makes cleaning easy for a caregiver. The listing gives no cup count or dimensions in the text we have.

Compared with the OTHWAY it cites a standard but gives fewer numbers, and compared with the GORILLA GRIP square it is aimed at tubs. It suits a buyer who wants a documented test reference and a soft surface. If you read the test statement, look for the date and the lab on the product page, since those details tell you how recent it is.
products.bestFor: A mat with a named slip-test reference and a soft surface.
cons: Cup count and dimensions are not stated in the text we have

products.name: TEESHLY Non Slip Bath Tub and Shower Mat, 40 x 16 Inch
products.description:
TEESHLY's 40 by 16 inch mat covers more of a long tub, with a domed pebble-like surface, soft-touch PVC and drain holes, and it is machine washable. The extra length gives an older adult more room to place a foot and fewer bare patches at the ends of the tub floor. The listing calls it especially suitable for a safe bathing experience.

Coverage helps with stepping in and out, because a wider landing area means less precision is needed. The domed surface adds a massage feel, which some people enjoy and others find too bumpy underfoot. The listing does not state a cup count in the text we have, so confirm the grip details on the product page.

Compared with the OTHWAY it is longer but states fewer numbers, and compared with the Hargiis it is firmer and has a suction-style grip. It suits a long tub where a bigger landing area is welcome. A big mat is also easy to see from a standing position, which helps anyone with limited vision.
products.bestFor: A larger landing area in a long tub.
pros: 40 in length covers more of the tub
cons: Cup count is not stated in the text we have
Domes may feel bumpy to some feet
Long mat may not suit a short tub

products.name: homerella Non Slip Bathtub Mat, 35x16, Over 250 Suction Cups
products.description:
homerella lists over 250 suction cups on a 35 by 16 inch mat with a machine-washable, mildew-resistant, odorless material, and describes it as made for everyone including older adults. More cups mean more points of contact, which helps hold the mat on a smooth floor. A cold machine wash makes cleaning easy for a caregiver.

The odorless material matters for people sensitive to the smell of new rubber, and the mildew-resistant description is helpful in a damp bathroom. The antibacterial claims are the maker's wording. The listing does not state a drain hole count in the text we have.

Compared with the OTHWAY it has more cups but fewer stated holes, and compared with the GORILLA GRIP square it is a tub mat. It suits a household that wants a high cup count and an easy wash routine. If the mat has been in storage, wash it before first use, since dust on the cups weakens the seal.
products.bestFor: A high cup count and a simple cold-wash routine.
cons: Antibacterial claims are the maker's wording
Drain hole count is not stated in the text we have

buyingCriteria.explanation: A curling edge is a trip hazard, especially for someone who shuffles. A square stall mat like the GORILLA GRIP stays away from the walls, and a flexible TPE mat like the OTHWAY lies flat. Press each edge down after placing the mat and check that it stays. If an edge lifts, choose a different size or retire the mat.

The Hargiis is 0.4 inch thick with a soft foam top, the TEESHLY has domed bumps and the GORILLA GRIP has pebble texture. Tender or older soles may prefer soft over bumpy. Stand on a similar surface at home, such as a thick towel, to judge. Comfort affects whether people keep the mat in place.

A clear or white mat on a white tub can be hard to see, which matters if vision is not sharp. Choose a color that contrasts with the tub floor, such as a darker mat on a light tub. The GORILLA GRIP is offered in clear, beige and black, and others vary. A visible mat also tells you at a glance whether it has shifted.

The OTHWAY and homerella list 198 and over 250 suction cups, while the Hargiis relies on a patterned backing. Cups need smooth surfaces, and patterned backings depend on friction. Match the mechanism to your floor and test the grip before each shower. A mat that has shifted should be reset.

The homerella and TEMIR list machine washing, and the Hargiis rinses clean with a spray. A mat that is easy to wash is one that gets washed, which matters for hygiene and for the cups' hold. Wash on cold and hang dry. Lift the mat after each shower.

A stall needs a square like the 21 by 21 inch GORILLA GRIP, and a tub needs a long mat like the 40-inch TEESHLY or the 35-inch homerella. A mat that is too big curls at the walls and one too small leaves gaps. Measure the flat floor, not the top of the tub. Measure twice, then add a small margin at each end, because a mat that touches the tub walls tends to curl.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stay-put design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared suction cup counts, such as 198 on the OTHWAY and over 250 on the homerella, and the patterned backing on the Hargiis. We read the stated surface limits. Grip claims were weighed with caution. We looked at each listing through the eyes of a caregiver, who buys, washes and checks the mat.

howWeEvaluated.title: Comfort underfoot
howWeEvaluated.description: Surfaces were compared: the soft 0.4-inch Hargiis, the domed TEESHLY and the pebble GORILLA GRIP. We considered tender feet. Softer, forgiving surfaces earned credit. Visibility against the tub was treated as part of safety, since a mat you cannot see is hard to check.

howWeEvaluated.title: Visibility and edges
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered color options, edge behavior and shape, from the square stall mat to long tub mats. A mat you can see and that lies flat is safer. Where the grip depends on the floor, we said so, and credited makers who say it too.

howWeEvaluated.title: Caregiver cleaning
howWeEvaluated.description: Machine washing, rinse cleaning and drying were compared. Easy cleaning earned credit because it keeps the mat hygienic and gripping. Cushioning was weighed as a reason someone might keep using the mat, not merely as a comfort extra.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claims honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: The TEMIR ASTM F462 statement and antibacterial wording were read as maker claims. Listings that note surface limits earned credit. We considered how heavy and bulky each mat is to lift, since weekly washing is part of ownership.

howToChoose.intro: Tiers are relative and use no price figures.
Mats hold the floor in two different ways, and the floor decides which works.

cards.label: Cup-based grip
cards.text: OTHWAY, homerella, TEMIR, TEESHLY and the GORILLA GRIP square all push air out from under cups and rely on a smooth, sealed floor. They are the usual answer for a clean glazed tub. If the floor is textured they will not seal.

cards.label: Backing-based grip
cards.text: Hargiis leans on a plaid-patterned underside and friction rather than a stated cup count. It suits someone who wants a soft, thick mat and is ready to test how well it holds on their own tub before trusting it.

howToChoose.note: Whichever you pick, give the mat a firm shove with your foot before the first real shower.

howToChoose.subheading: If Feet Are Tender or Balance Is Uncertain

cards.label: What to look for
cards.text: A top you can stand on comfortably for several minutes, edges that sit flat when pressed, a color that contrasts with the tub and a mat light enough to lift out and wash. Pair it with a screwed-in grab bar and bright lighting.

cards.label: How these picks line up
cards.text: Hargiis is the softest, the GORILLA GRIP square is the flattest in a stall, and the OTHWAY and homerella spread their hold across the most cups. None of them replaces a handhold.

faq.q: What shower mat is best for an older adult?
faq.a: One that stays put, lies flat, is easy to see and is simple to wash. The OTHWAY and homerella give high cup counts, the Hargiis is the most cushioned and the GORILLA GRIP square suits stalls. Pair the mat with a grab bar. If you notice the edges lifting after a few weeks, wash the mat and the floor, since oil from soap and bath products is the usual culprit.

faq.q: Should the mat be a contrasting color?
faq.a: It helps. A mat that contrasts with the tub floor is easier to see, which is useful if vision is not sharp. Many mats come in several colors. Check that you can see the edges. Ask the person using the mat whether the surface feels comfortable, because a mat that bothers their feet may be quietly removed.

faq.q: Can a mat prevent a fall?
faq.a: No product can promise that. A mat reduces slipping underfoot when it is properly placed and gripping. Use a grab bar, good lighting and careful stepping. It is helpful to keep a spare mat of the same type so that one can dry while the other is in use.

faq.q: How do I keep the mat from moving?
faq.a: Clean the tub floor, press the mat down and let it settle. Lift it after each shower so the cups reseal. If it still shifts, the surface may not suit suction. When someone else helps with bathing, they can check the mat's grip and edges before each use in a few seconds.

Machine wash on cold if the listing allows, as with the homerella and TEMIR, or rinse and scrub with mild soap. Hang to dry. A caregiver can do this weekly. If the mat slides even on a smooth floor, replace it, because a worn mat can lose its hold even when it looks fine.

It is softer, as with the 0.4 inch Hargiis, but may grip differently. Thick mats can also be bulkier to step over. Test the edges for flatness. A bath bench or a handheld shower can make bathing easier alongside a mat, and a therapist can advise on a full setup.
